feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x)=3{(\frac{1}{5})}^{2x-1}+7.$ Given that $f(x)\to a$ as $x\to \infty ,$ then $a=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's plot the graph of $y=f(x):$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943819/assets/a3e317bdf1d7c1da85a164331d61dc1500af980ef2b3e907098dd19f42287d8c.png)

Since the function approaches the line $y=7$ as $x\to \infty ,$ we conclude that

$$
f(x)\to 7\,\text{as}\,x\to \infty .
$$

Therefore, $a=7.$
